title: First bands, saxophone then clarinet, jazz as a hobby
summary: He played with anyone, bought a saxophone at fifteen without lessons, took up clarinet at eighteen, and treated music as a hobby since Australia offered no financial scene.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Well, uh, was Frank Johnson the first band you played with, or you played with Elie Wilhoff?
Uh, the first recognized band. I, I played, played about with anyone and everyone, uh, wherever I could. Um.
Well, I started on, on saxophone, but dropped that, uh, after a few years, uh, and decided the clarinet was, uh, a better instrument, and, uh, the clarinet I was, uh, tried to play.
Uh, what age were you when you took up saxophone?

Well, I bought me a saxophone when I was fifteen. Mm-hm. Just used to, uh, blow about on it. I never had lessons, which was a bad thing. It took so much longer to, uh, get anywhere. Um, I was eighteen, I suppose, when I took up, uh, clarinet.

It was always just very much of a secondary type of hobby. Mm-hm. And, uh, there's nothing, uh, there's no great musical scene in Australia to, uh, make it worthwhile financially to, uh, try and, uh, break into anything.
